levelDefinitions.L1 conceptual: phase document exists with >= 8 distinct engineering sections AND a kernel phase contract exists
levelDefinitions.L2 data model: phase document carries data-model vocabulary AND (a migration references the capability OR the contract declares substrates)
levelDefinitions.L3 backend: every declared module resolves to real source AND every contract-cited test file exists with >= 1 real test
levelDefinitions.L4 frontend/workspace integration: at least one route or component references the phase's modules or capability
levelDefinitions.L5 operational maturity: an operational artifact (proof, verifier, CI job, runbook or infrastructure file) names the phase or capability

limitations: Evidence-derived: this audit measures artefacts, not correctness of behaviour.

L4 requires a DISTINCTIVE reference: the capability id inside a surface, or a route/component importing the phase's module directly. A bare module word is not credited ("identity" used to match marketing prose and inflated three phases), and an INDIRECT projection (surface → server function → module) is not credited either, so L4 may UNDERSTATE a phase — the safe direction; close by hand review with recorded evidence.
DB-backed L2 registries are verified by scripts/verify-l2-registries.mjs, which requires live Supabase credentials.
Incompleteness is reported, never failed: unfinished work is honest. Only overstated claims or missing cited artifacts fail the gate.
